title: Senior's toolkit: GitHub Actions workflows
summary: The workflow keys and tools experienced people use: dispatch inputs, concurrency, permissions, timeouts, step outputs, actionlint and act.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: GitHub Actions workflows
steps.body: Most workflow trouble comes from a few keys left out (no timeout, no concurrency, default permissions) and from YAML pushed without a check. These fix that.

toolkit.what: Adds a "Run workflow" button and `gh workflow run` support, with typed inputs. Every deploy workflow should have one.
flags: the run cannot start without it
toolkit.example:
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]
        required: true

toolkit.what: Allows one run per group at a time. On pull requests, cancel the old run when a new commit arrives; on deploys, queue instead.
flags: one group per workflow and branch
stop the older run (never for production deploys)

toolkit.what: Limits what the job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can do. Start from read-only and grant per job only what that job needs.
flags: request an OIDC token for keyless cloud login
toolkit.example:
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  publish:
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

toolkit.what: Kills a hung job. The default is 360 minutes, so one stuck test can burn six hours of runner time.
Sets a step output that later steps and jobs can read. (The old `::set-output` command is deprecated and prints warnings.)
flags: read it in the same job
map it so other jobs can use `needs.<job>.outputs.version`

toolkit.what: Writes Markdown to the run's summary page: a test table, the image digest, a deploy link. Reviewers see it without opening logs.
flags: headings, tables and links all render

toolkit.what: Lints workflow files: unknown keys, bad expressions, wrong `needs`, and shellcheck on `run:` scripts. Catches the typo before you push and wait.
toolkit.when: before every push that touches a workflow

toolkit.what: Runs workflow jobs locally in Docker containers. Good for fast iteration on scripts; not identical to GitHub's runners (other images, no OIDC).
flags: provide secrets from a local file

steps.prompt: A job that normally takes 6 minutes shows as still running after 5 hours. A test is stuck waiting on a socket. What stops this from happening again?
steps.explain: The default job timeout is 360 minutes. A timeout a bit above the normal duration fails fast and frees the runner. Concurrency only cancels when a newer run starts.

steps.prompt: Match the key to what it does.
pairs: stop the older run when a newer one starts in the group
let this job push images to GHCR
let this job request an OIDC token
pass a value to later steps

steps.prompt: Cancel superseded runs on the same branch.
steps.explain: `max-parallel` and `fail-fast` belong to `strategy:` for matrices; they do not cancel other runs.

steps.prompt: In job `build`, step `meta` runs `echo "version=1.4.2" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`, and a later step in `build` prints it fine. But job `deploy` (with `needs: build`) gets an empty string from `${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}`. What is missing?
options: An `outputs:` map on the `build` job: `version: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}`
steps.explain: Step outputs stay inside their job until the job maps them in `jobs.build.outputs`. `$GITHUB_ENV` only reaches later steps of the same job, and expressions that point at a missing output quietly give an empty string.

steps.prompt: Put the edit loop for a workflow change in order.
steps.explain: Lint and run locally first, so each round trip to GitHub tests a real change instead of a typo.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Every workflow you write gets `permissions:`, `timeout-minutes:` and a `concurrency:` group, and every edit goes through `actionlint` before it is pushed. Put the useful results in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` so nobody has to read logs to know what shipped.
